title: Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) Registration Requirements and Review Standards
content:
Registration in the Extended Care Health Option (ECHO) rests on the same standards in all ten tiers, from Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor E-1 to E-5 through Extended Care Health Option, Sponsor O-9 and O-10. The tiers differ only in the sponsor pay grades they cover and the monthly cost share; the registration standards below apply to every tier without variation.

## 1. Who may register

**1.1 Eligible DEERS beneficiary categories (every tier):**
- active duty family member
- transitional survivor

**1.2 Qualifying conditions that support registration (every tier):**
- moderate or severe intellectual disability
- serious physical disability
- extraordinary physical or psychological condition
- neuromuscular developmental condition
- multiple disabilities

## 2. Programme requirements

| Requirement | Every tier |
|---|---|
| The sponsor must have the beneficiary enrolled in the service's Exceptional Family Member Program | yes |
| An ECHO case manager must be assigned before any ECHO service | yes |
| The beneficiary must hold TRICARE Prime or TRICARE Select coverage | yes |

## 3. Registration file and decision

| Standard | Every tier |
|---|---|
| Documents a registration must include | a diagnosis from a TRICARE-authorized provider; the Exceptional Family Member Program enrollment confirmation |
| Business days within which a complete registration is decided | 10 |
| Date the registration takes effect | the date the case manager approves the registration |
| Months between case-manager recertifications of the qualifying condition | 12 |

## Points of application

- **Both documents belong to a registration.** A registration includes the diagnosis from a TRICARE-authorized provider and the Exceptional Family Member Program enrollment confirmation; the 10-business-day decision period is stated for a complete registration.
- **The effective date is the approval date.** The registration does not take effect on the date the request was received; it takes effect on the date the case manager approves it.
- **Recertification recurs.** The case manager recertifies the qualifying condition every 12 months.
- **A beneficiary category outside the list.** A DEERS category other than active duty family member or transitional survivor is not among the eligible categories of any tier.

*Hypothetical example, for illustration only:* a registration request is received on one date and the case manager approves it on a later date within the 10 business days; the registration takes effect on the approval date, not on the date of receipt.
